source.title: tryToParseJwt() accepts tokens with an empty signature segment

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
## 现象

`tryToParseJwt()` in `packages/workflow/src/type-validation.ts` validates a token with:

```ts
const jwtPattern = /^[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_.+/=]*$/;
```

The third (signature) segment uses `*` (zero or more), so it also matches an empty string. A string such as `header.payload.` therefore passes validation and is returned as a valid JWT, even though a JWT must contain a non-empty signature segment.

## 最小复现

```ts
import { tryToParseJwt } from 'n8n-workflow';

tryToParseJwt('header.payload.'); // returns 'header.payload.' instead of throwing
tryToParseJwt('a.b.');            // returns 'a.b.' instead of throwing
```

## 期望

The signature segment should require at least one character (`+` instead of `*`). Tokens with an empty signature must be rejected with a `UserError`, while normal three-segment tokens continue to be accepted unchanged.

## 影响

`tryToParseJwt` is used to validate `jwt`-typed field values. Accepting a truncated or malformed token (a copy/paste mistake, or a crafted value) lets an invalid, credential-like string pass validation and flow into downstream nodes. It then either fails later with a much less clear error or is sent to an API as a malformed `Authorization` token.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The current source still uses `*` for the signature segment in `packages/workflow/src/type-validation.ts`, so `header.payload.` matches and is returned. Requiring one or more signature characters (`+`) would reject this truncated form while leaving the existing three-segment check intact. Note that this remains a shape check, not cryptographic signature verification.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The current `type-validation.ts` still uses `*` for the signature segment, so `header.payload.` passes the shape check. Changing it to `+` addresses the empty-segment case. One nuance: JWT permits an empty signature for the unsecured `alg: "none"` form, so if this validator intends to accept only signed tokens, that restriction should be explicit; otherwise the regex change also rejects that valid serialization.
